title: Review: Magnetic materials, domains and permeability; Fields of currents (quantitative); Force on moving charges; Force on a current-carrying conductor; Magnetic flux and Faraday's/Lenz's laws; Motional emf and generators; Reflection and refraction
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics 2 (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: W04-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; MG03-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; MG03-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; MG06-1#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: MG02-1#N.13, MG03-1#N.3a, MG04-1#N.5, MG06-1#N.14, MG07-1#N.4, NEW-magnetic-materials-1#N.2, W04-1#N.13b, MG02-1#N.3a, MG03-1#N.12b, MG04-1#N.14, MG06-1#N.6b, MG07-1#N.3a. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Wavefront
items.clue: Line or surface joining points that are in phase, such as every crest.

items.label: Kinetic energy
items.clue: Quantity of a moving charge that a magnetic push leaves unchanged, like its speed.

items.label: Work
items.clue: Never done by the magnetic push on a moving charge, as it acts at 90° to the velocity.

items.label: Eddy currents
items.clue: Induced flows of charge around inside a solid metal sheet or pipe, opposing the motion.

questions.stem: A long straight wire carries a current vertically upwards. It is in a uniform horizontal magnetic field that points due north. In which direction is the magnetic force on the wire?

options.text: Due east
Due west
Due south
Vertically downwards

questions.explanation: The force is at right angles to both the current (up) and the field (north), so it is horizontal, east or west; the rule gives west.

questions.stem: An electron moves toward the right side of the page through a uniform magnetic field directed out of the page. What is the direction of the magnetic force exerted on the electron at this instant?

options.text: Toward the top of the page
Toward the bottom of the page
Out of the page, along B
Left, opposite its motion

questions.stem: Two long straight parallel wires, 1 and 2, are a distance d apart. Wire 1 carries a current I, and wire 2 carries a current 3I in the same direction. Point P is on the line joining the wires, between them, at the location where the net magnetic field produced by the two wires is zero. Ignore Earth's magnetic field. Which expression gives the distance from wire 1 to P?

A thick aluminium plate swings as a pendulum through the gap between the poles of a strong magnet, and stops after a few swings. An identical plate with many deep slots cut into it swings for much longer. Which explains the difference?

options.text: Aluminium is attracted by magnets, and the solid plate has more metal for the magnet to grip.
Currents induced in the moving solid plate oppose its motion; the slots block their paths.
The slots let air pass through the plate, so the slotted plate meets far less air resistance.
The induced currents draw energy from the magnet, which grows weaker during each swing of the solid plate.

questions.stem: Use Lenz's law to predict before the next screen. A metal rod rests across two horizontal conducting rails that are joined at one end by a resistor, in a uniform vertical magnetic field. A student gives the rod a brief push along the rails and lets go. Friction and air resistance are negligible. Which claim about the rod's motion after the push, with its justification, is correct?

options.text: It speeds up, because the force on its induced current points along its motion.
It keeps a constant speed, because a steady, uniform field induces no current.
It slows down, because its induced current feels a magnetic force opposing its motion.
It stops at once, because nothing pushes it forward once the push ends.

questions.stem: Which of the following produces a magnetic field? Ignore Earth's field and Earth's motion.

options.text: A charged plastic ring held at rest on a stand
A charged plastic ring spinning about its central axis
An uncharged copper ring spinning about its central axis
An unmagnetized iron ring, held at rest on a stand

questions.stem: A ray of light in air strikes a flat block of plastic P at an angle of incidence of 40°. The same ray then strikes a flat block of a different plastic, Q, at the same angle of incidence. The ray changes direction by a larger angle as it enters P than as it enters Q. Which conclusion can be drawn from this observation?

options.text: Light travels more slowly in plastic P than in plastic Q.
Light travels faster in plastic P than in plastic Q.
Plastic P has a larger mass density than plastic Q.
Light travels at the same speed in P as it does in Q.

questions.stem: A straight wire in the plane of the page carries a current toward the right side of the page through a uniform magnetic field directed into the page. What is the direction of the magnetic force exerted on the wire?

options.text: Toward the bottom edge of the page
Into the page, along the field
Rightward, along the current
Toward the top edge of the page

questions.stem: A proton moves at 2.0 × 10⁴ m/s toward the right side of the page through a region that contains a uniform electric field of magnitude 3.0 × 10³ N/C directed toward the bottom of the page and a uniform magnetic field of magnitude 0.050 T directed into the page. The gravitational force on the proton is negligible. What is the magnitude of the net force exerted on the proton at this instant? (Use e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.)
A light, loosely wound coil of wire, like a soft spring, hangs vertically. A large steady current is passed through it. What happens to the length of the coil?

options.text: It gets shorter: neighbouring turns carry current the same way, so they attract.
It gets longer, because neighbouring turns carry like currents, and like currents repel.
It stays the same, because the coil's own field cannot exert a force on the coil itself.
It gets longer, because the field inside the coil pushes the turns apart along its axis.

questions.explanation: Each turn is like a parallel wire beside the next, with current the same way: they pull together and the coil contracts.

questions.stem: A square wire loop with sides of 0.15 m lies in a horizontal plane in a uniform vertical magnetic field. The field's magnitude increases steadily from 0.20 T to 0.60 T in 0.12 s. What is the magnitude of the emf induced in the loop?

A metal rod slides at a constant 2.0 m/s along two parallel horizontal conducting rails that are 0.25 m apart. The rails are joined at one end by a 0.50 Ω resistor; the rod and rails have negligible resistance. A uniform 0.40 T magnetic field is perpendicular to the plane of the rails. At the instant the rod is 0.50 m from the resistor, what is the current in the resistor?
